brief: Viết một bài ngắn 250-400 từ bằng tiếng Việt giới thiệu cách merchant Việt Nam nhận thanh toán USDC qua cơ chế CCTP (burn-and-mint của Circle). deliverable:
Accepting USDC as a Vietnamese merchant: how CCTP actually works

Imagine Ms. Hoa, who sells silk in Hoi An. A customer wants to pay in USDC held on Ethereum, but Ms. Hoa keeps her funds on Arc, where fees are negligible. Moving value between two blockchains normally requires a bridge — a third party that locks your money and issues an IOU token, with all the risk that implies.

CCTP (Cross-Chain Transfer Protocol), built by Circle — the issuer of USDC itself — takes a different route called burn-and-mint. When the customer confirms payment, their USDC is permanently destroyed (burned) on the source chain. Circle attests that the burn happened, and the exact same amount is minted directly into Ms. Hoa's wallet on the destination chain. No locked funds, no wrapped tokens, no change in total USDC supply.

A concrete transaction looks like this: the customer signs two actions in their wallet (an approval, then the burn). The merchant's gateway software watches for Circle's attestation and completes the mint automatically. With Fast Transfer, the whole cycle takes roughly 60 to 120 seconds — fast enough for an in-store checkout. The protocol fee is about 0.01%, deducted at mint time.

The part that matters for a shop owner: none of this machinery is her problem. She needs a wallet address and a QR code; the gateway handles attestations, contract calls, and retries. The USDC lands in a wallet only she controls — no intermediary can freeze or custody it. Her job stays the same as it has always been: sell silk, and reconcile the balance at the end of the day.
